meta.title: Improve Scheme backend count builtin
meta.body_summary: Optimize code generation for the count builtin in the Scheme compiler by changing compiler.go and regenerating test outputs.

perf_labels.notes: Single-commit compiler optimization merged instantly by author with no review or performance evidence; no benchmark or repro steps provided.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 923 changed lines across 107 files, this is a medium-sized change by absolute volume. However, only 7 lines were actually changed in compiler.go; the vast majority are regenerated test outputs, some with large deletions (220 lines each) and others with trivial 1-line updates. This fits a small compiler optimization that was merged instantly without review.

review_details.performance_claim: Optimizing code generation for the count builtin in the Scheme compiler backend.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: In an author-maintained repository, an agent-produced compiler optimization can be merged instantly without any review or performance evidence, relying solely on the author's trust and the passing of existing tests.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark, profiling data, or reproducible performance improvement steps are provided; only a commit message and a test command.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No review or regression issues were raised.

core_change_summary.description: Modified compiler/x/scheme/compiler.go with 7 additions to change the code generation for the count builtin. All other changes are regenerated machine outputs (*.scm files) that reflect this compiler update, along with minor updates to .out files and TASKS.md.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: 106 test files were regenerated, with most having 1-2 line diffs; three files had large deletions of 220 lines each.
change_trajectory: Single commit (2316fe1) modified compiler.go and regenerated all affected Scheme machine test outputs.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened and instantly merged by the author with no review or human interaction.
